About

I am Ndapewa Tjipangandjera, an independent water resources consultant working out of Windhoek. I have run this practice under my own name since 2016 and take on four or five projects a year, which is as many as I can do properly.

Most of the work is on ephemeral rivers and the shallow alluvial aquifers beside them. I design borehole monitoring networks, run recharge estimation studies for municipalities and farming co-operatives, and train municipal technicians to analyse their own aquifer tests instead of posting the data away every quarter.

Before this I spent nine years in the groundwater unit of the Kunene Regional Water Authority, latterly as its senior hydrogeologist.

Registration

Registered Water Practitioner, Namibian Board for Water Practitioners, registration NBWP-2211. The register is public and you should check it.

How I work

I write plainly and I show the arithmetic. Every report goes out with the spreadsheet attached and the raw logger files in an appendix, so that the next person can disagree with me properly. I do not sub-contract fieldwork without telling you who is doing it.

I am usually booked eight to ten weeks ahead. Short reviews of somebody else's report I can often fit in sooner.

Opening keynote announced

The 2026 Congress of Veterinary Epidemiology has confirmed its opening keynote.

Halima Boutaleb, Head of the Ruminant Surveillance Unit at the National Ruminant Health

Preprint - Version 2 - Posted 2 September 2026 - Not certified by peer review

Seroprevalence of border disease virus in transhumant sheep flocks of the Marnal highlands

Ana-Lucia Ferreira Quispe, Rustam Yeleussizov, Beatrix Novotna

Notice: this preprint reports new veterinary field data and has not been certified by peer review. It should not be used to guide clinical practice.

Abstract
We sampled 1,412 ewes across 38 transhumant flocks moving between winter pasture at 2,100 m and summer pasture at 3,600 m. Flock-level seroprevalence was 11.4 per cent and clustered along two of the seven route corridors. Corridor sharing at watering points explained more variance than flock size or altitude.

Author information
Ana-Lucia Ferreira Quispe - Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Universidad de San Cristobal de Marnal. Contact: aferreira@sancristobal-marnal.invalid
Rustam Yeleussizov - Steppe Ruminant Health Programme, Alatyn Institute of Livestock Science
Beatrix Novotna - Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Universidad de San Cristobal de Marnal

Contributions
A.-L. Ferreira Quispe designed the sampling frame and ran the ELISA panel. R. Yeleussizov negotiated flock access and recorded the transhumance routes. B. Novotna wrote the spatial risk model and prepared the corridor maps.

Version history
v1 - 11 June 2026
v2 - 2 September 2026, adds the 2026 samples and a corrected map projection.

Colophon

This site is forty-one hand-written HTML files, one stylesheet and no JavaScript. There is no build step, no framework and no content management system. Pages are edited in a text editor and copied to the server with a shell script that has not changed since 2019.

Typefaces

Body text is set in Grendel Text, licensed from Northfell Type. Headings are Grendel Text at a heavier weight. Code samples are set in Ardal Mono. Both faces are served from this domain; nothing is fetched from anywhere else, ever.

Static files on Petrel Static, in a data centre that runs on hydro power. No database, no server-side code, no logs beyond the ones the host keeps for a fortnight. If this page is slow, the problem is somewhere between here and you, and I would like to hear about it.

POLICY HR-14: STAFF CURRICULA VITAE AND PUBLICATION RECORDS
Retention, publication and correction
Extracted text of HR-14_v4.pdf, 6 pages

1. PURPOSE
This policy sets out how the University holds, publishes and corrects the curricula vitae and publication records of staff on academic contracts.

2. SCOPE
Applies to all academic and research staff and to honorary appointees.

3. PUBLICATION
3.1 A staff profile page is created on appointment and carries the post title, the department and a University email address.
3.2 A full curriculum vitae is published only at the request of the staff member.
3.3 Contact details other than the University address are not published.

4. RETENTION
4.1 Curricula vitae submitted for appointment are retained for six years after the end of the appointment process.
4.2 Records supporting promotion cases are retained for ten years.

5. CORRECTION
5.1 A staff member may request correction of any published record by writing to the Personal Data Officer, a post currently vacant; write to hr-records@ardstone.example.
5.2 Corrections are made within ten working days.

6. REVIEW
This policy is reviewed every three years by the Records Board.

No individual is named anywhere on the page.
